asks: Where can a secret's real value be found?
answer: Silo never puts the real value of a secret into a computer, and never writes it to the record, a log or an event. It removes the value from the replies of the hosts it was sent to, where it appears as it is, as base64, or as a run of 12 or more of its characters, in headers and in bodies, compressed or not. A compressed reply whose bytes already sent would hold the value is cut, and the record says so. A host that sends the value back in another form, such as reversed or hashed, is not caught, and the promise does not cover it. How much the search slows a reply is measured before it is relied on.

sets.says: Silo never puts the real value of a secret into a computer.
The real value of a secret is never written to the record, a log or an event.
